result.summary: The hymn's speaker announces a song to Zeus, the greatest and all-seeing lord of the gods, who counsels with Themis. The speaker then asks him to be gracious.

scenes.title: Invocation of Zeus
scenes.summary: The singer praises Zeus as chief of the gods, shown whispering wisdom to Themis, and begs his favour.

notable_quotes.reason: Concise opening praising Zeus as supreme and wise, in counsel with Themis.

analysis.text: The hymn presents Zeus as supreme ruler whose power is joined with wisdom and justice, shown by his closeness to Themis, goddess of right order.
Like other short Homeric Hymns, it works as a brief prayer or proem, perhaps used to open a recitation.

fun_facts.text: This hymn is only four lines long, one of the shortest in the collection.

language_notes.text: "Fulfiller" translates the idea that Zeus brings plans and decrees to completion; nothing he ordains fails.
"Leaning towards him" depicts Themis sitting close and attentive, as a counsellor would, while Zeus speaks quietly to her.
"Be gracious" is a formal prayer request, asking the god to look kindly on the singer and the song.

context_notes.text: Themis is the goddess of divine law, custom and right order. In Hesiod she is a Titan, and she is counted among the wives of Zeus.
"Son of Cronos" refers to Zeus's father, the Titan Cronos, whom Zeus overthrew to become ruler of the gods.

literary_notes.text: Stacked titles (chiefest, greatest, all-seeing, lord of all) characterize Zeus by his power and knowledge, as in the formulaic style of hymns.
The singer turns from third-person narration to address Zeus directly, closing the hymn with a personal plea and repeating "all-seeing" as a frame.
